- When sentiment is positive (≥0.17) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce the forecast peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and forecast is falling, avoid overcorrecting downward — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- In high-sentiment environments, model tends to overestimate short-term volatility — cap 30d forecast max at 1.5x recent 18d high.  
- If recent 18d price is trending up and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often underestimates continuation — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.17), model overfits noise — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5 values before final output.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid mean reversion overcorrection.  
- In low-sentiment (≤0.06) environments, model often underestimates downside risk — add 0.3–0.8 to forecast if sentiment is flat or negative.
